events.uncertainty: Whether this attachment is permanent or later removed.

events.description: The person detaches the assembled transport cabin and chassis unit from the main assembly.
events.uncertainty: The reason for detaching the cabin after assembly.

events.description: The person holds the detached cabin and uses a yellow tool to interact with its interior.
events.uncertainty: The specific function of the yellow tool on the interior.

events.description: The person uses the yellow tool to secure the white cabin back onto the orange chassis.
events.uncertainty: The completion status of the re-attachment.

events.description: The person flips the unit over and places a small white sticker onto the bottom.
events.uncertainty: The content or purpose of the sticker.

events.description: Participant holds an orange rectangular panel, examining it before placing it onto the top of the truck cab.
events.uncertainty: Exact attachment mechanism not fully visible.

events.description: Participant reaches toward the table with the left hand, possibly adjusting the cab or retrieving a part.
events.uncertainty: Target of the hand movement is partially obscured.

events.description: Participant uses a yellow-handled screwdriver to fasten the orange panel onto the top of the cab.
events.uncertainty: Screwing action is repetitive; exact screw count unclear.

events.uncertainty: Transition from previous state to this assembly is not shown.

events.description: Participant holds the truck vertically, using the screwdriver to attach a grey part to the cab side.
events.uncertainty: Specific part name and its necessity are not visible.

events.description: The person holds a yellow-handled screwdriver and positions it over a black wheel on the orange device.
events.uncertainty: Specific detachment action not yet completed.

events.description: The person rotates the screwdriver on the black wheel and then moves the tool away from the device.
events.uncertainty: Whether the wheel was detached or re-attached is unclear.

inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.
